test_title: PYST 53: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 21 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The magnification of a concave mirror is −1. Which of the following statements is correct about the position of the object?

options.text: Object is beyond the centre of curvature
Object is between focus and pole
Object is at the centre of curvature

solution:
The correct answer is __**Object is at the centre of curvature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **magnification (m)** of a spherical mirror is defined as the ratio of the **height of the image (h')** to the **height of the object (h)**. It is also expressed in terms of **object distance (u)** and **image distance (v)** as **m = -v/u**.
 
• In this question, the **magnification is -1**. The **negative sign** indicates that the image formed is **real and inverted**. ***Hence, the image is formed in front of the mirror.***
 
• The **numerical value 1** indicates that the **size of the image is exactly equal to the size of the object** (|v| = |u|).
 
• For a **concave mirror**, the image is of the **same size** as the object only when the object is placed at the **centre of curvature (C)**. In this specific case, the image is also formed at the **centre of curvature**, is **real**, and is **inverted**. ***Hence, the statement "Object is at the centre of curvature" is correct.***
 
• If the **object is beyond the centre of curvature**, the image is formed between the **focus (F)** and the **centre of curvature (C)** and is **diminished** (|m| 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror:** It is a **spherical mirror** whose reflecting surface is curved inwards, towards the centre of the sphere. It is also known as a **converging mirror** because it converges light rays that fall on it.
 
• **Mirror Formula:** The relationship between the **focal length (f)**, **object distance (u)**, and **image distance (v)** is given by the formula: **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**.
 
• **Sign Convention:** According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the pole (P) of the mirror is taken as the origin. The **object distance (u)** is always **negative**. For a **concave mirror**, the **focal length (f)** and the **radius of curvature (R)** are always **negative**.
 
• **Radius of Curvature (R):** The distance between the **pole** and the **centre of curvature** is called the radius of curvature. It is related to the focal length by the equation **R = 2f**.
 
• **Uses of Concave Mirrors:** They are commonly used in **shaving mirrors** to see a larger image of the face, in **torches** and **searchlights** to get powerful parallel beams of light, and by **dentists** to see large images of teeth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• If **m is positive**, the image is **virtual and erect**.
 
• If **m is negative**, the image is **real and inverted**.
 
• If **|m| > 1**, the image is **enlarged**.
 
• If **|m| < 1**, the image is **diminished**.
 
• If **|m| = 1**, the image is of the **same size** as the object.
 
• A **plane mirror** always has a magnification of **+1**, meaning the image is virtual, erect, and of the same size as the object.
 
• A **convex mirror** always produces a **virtual, erect, and diminished** image, so its magnification is always **positive and less than 1**.
